summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after being found unresponsive at home with severe back pain, hypotension, and hypoxia. She was intubated in the field due to suspected STEMI and VT. In the hospital, she was diagnosed with cardiogenic shock, hypoxic respiratory failure, and a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli. She required an intra-aortic balloon pump and vasopressors, which were later weaned. Imaging revealed a left atrial appendage thrombus, multifocal pneumonia, and stable spinal compression fractures. She was treated with antibiotics, anticoagulation, and supportive care. Her mental status improved, and she was successfully extubated. Liver and kidney dysfunction resolved. She developed transient nausea and diarrhea, both managed supportively. After stabilization, she was discharged to a rehabilitation facility for deconditioning with plans for close cardiology and transplant team follow-up.
